chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Mansour ibn Yunus, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
The one who prays an Obligatory Salat and follows up to another, so he is a guest of Allah, and has a right upon Allah that He be Benevolent with His guest.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for performing an obligatory prayer followed immediately by another?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from al-Kafi highlights the spiritual merit of *muwābaqah* (immediate succession) in prayer, transforming the act into a state of divine hospitality. It underscores the concept that consistent devotion obligates Allah’s generosity, reinforcing the believer's reliance on divine grace (*karām*) rather than mere ritual completion.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Hadeed, from Mansour Bin Yunus, from the one who mentioned it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The one prays an Obligatory Salat and follows up to another, so he is a guest of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and has a right upon Allah<sup>azwj</sup> that He<sup>azwj</sup> be Benevolent with His<sup>azwj</sup> guest’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid from Manur ibn Yunus from those whom he has mentioned who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

If after completing an obligatory Salah (prayer), one remains in his place for ta‘qib (praying and speaking to Allah) up to the time of the next Salah (prayer), he is a guest of Allah and it is a right in his favor before Allah to honor His guest.’”
